title: Cards
summary: A Bootstrap card is a box that groups related content, such as one book title and its description.
introduction: A Bootstrap card is a box that groups related content, such as one book title and its description. Build one simple card before making a row of cards. Add a card body to give the words space from the edges.
learningObjectives: Assemble a card from card, card-body, card-title and card-text
Add images, headers, footers and list groups to a card
Lay out equal-height cards in a responsive grid
Colour cards with background and border utilities

blocks.text: `.card` is the box: a 1px border, `.375rem` rounded corners and a white background (in light mode). `.card-body` adds 1rem of padding and holds the content. Inside it, `.card-title` and `.card-subtitle` set heading margins, `.card-text` removes the bottom margin of the last paragraph, and `.card-link` spaces inline links. A card fills the width of its parent, so either give it a width or, more usually, place it in a grid column.

blocks.title: An event card
blocks.code:
Spring planting day

Saturday 21 March

Bring gloves and a trowel. Seedlings and tea are provided.

Details Sign up

blocks.title: Rendered result
blocks.content:
A 288px wide white box with a 1px light grey border and 6px rounded corners
Inside, with 16px padding all round: a 20px title, a 16px grey subtitle 8px below it, the paragraph, then two blue links on one line 16px apart

blocks.text: The headings use real `<h2>` and `<h3>` elements with `.h5` and `.h6` classes: the document outline stays correct while the visual size suits a small box. That is the pattern from the typography lesson applied to a component.

Cards have named regions that stack in source order. `.card-img-top` stretches an image to the card's width and rounds its top corners (`.card-img-bottom` does the same at the bottom). `.card-header` and `.card-footer` are tinted strips with their own padding. A `.list-group.list-group-flush` drops straight into the card with its side borders removed, so the rows line up with the card edges. Use any image file you have in place of `images/rose.jpg`.

blocks.content:
A very light grey "Featured" strip with a bottom border

blocks.text: To show several cards, put each in a grid column rather than giving cards widths. `row-cols-1 row-cols-md-3` yields one card per line on phones and three from tablets upward, and `g-4` spaces them. Columns in a row are already equal height, but the card inside a column is not: add `h-100` to each card so it stretches to its column, and short cards no longer leave ragged bottoms.

blocks.title: Three equal-height cards
blocks.code:
Short

One line.

Longer

This card has a longer description that wraps onto several lines, which would normally make it taller than its neighbours.

Medium

Two lines of text here.

blocks.title: Rendered result
blocks.content:
Below 768px: three cards stacked at full width, 24px apart
768px and wider: three cards on one line at one third each, 24px apart, all exactly as tall as the "Longer" card

blocks.text: A **horizontal card** is the same idea turned inward: a `row g-0` inside the card puts the image in one column and the body in another from the md breakpoint, and stacks them on phones.

blocks.title: Rendered result
blocks.content:
768px and wider: the image fills the left third of the card and the text the right two thirds, with no gap between them
Below 768px: the image sits above the text at the full card width

blocks.title: Common mistake: cards straight inside a row
blocks.text: A `.card` placed directly in a `.row`, without a `.col` wrapper, becomes a grid column itself: it is forced to 100% width and the row's gutter padding ends up *inside* its border, so the content is indented by 12px and every card fills the whole line. Always nest `row > col > card`. The same goes for `h-100`: it belongs on the card, not on the column, which is already full height.

Cards take the ordinary colour utilities. `text-bg-primary` sets a solid background **and** a readable text colour in one class, which is safer than pairing `bg-primary` with `text-white` by hand. `border-{colour}` tints only the border, usually combined with `text-{colour}` on the body for a subtle status card.

blocks.title: Make the whole card clickable
blocks.text: Add `stretched-link` to one link or button inside a card and the card's entire area becomes its click target, as long as the card has `position: relative` (which `.card` already does). Keep only one stretched link per card.

questions.question: Three cards in a row have different amounts of text. Which class on each card makes them equally tall?
questions.explanation: Columns in a flex row are already equal height; h-100 stretches the card to fill its column. w-100 would only change width and align-items-stretch is already the default.

questions.question: To show an image above the card's content, the `` goes before `.card-body` in the markup.
questions.explanation: Card regions stack in source order, so the image must precede the body. card-img-top also rounds the image's top corners to match the card.
